update_risk.title: A software update silently changes how the system works, breaking connected systems
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-085. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: adequate. Create R-LEO-AI-136
update_risk.hazard_description: The system that checks clinical software updates does not enforce version labelling rules. A new version of the software can be released with changes that break other connected systems. No warning is sent to the teams who rely on those connections. Clinical systems that feed patient information into care pathways may stop working correctly without anyone knowing.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A connected clinical system silently receives a breaking update. It begins to pull incorrect or incomplete information from patient records. A clinician reads the output and sees missing diagnoses, wrong medicines, or outdated care pathway information. The clinician does not know the information is wrong because no alert is shown.
update_risk.harm_description: A clinician acts on incomplete or incorrect patient information. A serious diagnosis may be missed or a wrong medicine may be given. The patient could be harmed as a result of a clinical decision based on information the system presented incorrectly.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: A version labelling policy requires every software release to be clearly numbered and any planned changes to be announced in advance before they take effect. The software development team applies this to every release (DI-DC8465F1). When a part of the system is due to change or be retired, the system automatically sends a warning notice to all connected teams and displays a sunset header so they can prepare. The software team manages this for every affected connection (DI-B0832A64). A dependency check runs automatically before any change is released. It confirms that no connected clinical rules or pathways will break. The software team runs this check on every release (DI-F1A768AE). Before any change that affects how information is displayed or recorded goes live, it must pass a review in a test environment, receive sign-off, be correctly versioned, and have a rollback plan ready. The software team and a clinical reviewer complete this before each release (DI-9FD54AD6). Every week, the system updates its list of clinical organisations and checks whether any of those updates would break existing connections. Any breaking change is blocked until it is resolved. The software team runs this check weekly (DI-634258FE). A permanent record of every change to patient information is kept for at least seven years. This record cannot be altered. The software team enforces this automatically for all records (DI-080A2454). The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs and test results for all these controls every quarter to confirm they are working as intended.

Guideline deprecation dependency closure enforcement
Surface form change gate: staging, review approval, versioning, and rollback
Weekly ODS synchronisation with blocking resolutions for breaking changes
Provenance record immutable retention policy enforcement (7-year minimum)

update_risk.title: System component instructions become incorrect or out of date
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-087. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: adequate. Create R-LEO-AI-137
update_risk.hazard_description: The instructions that tell different parts of the system how to share information may not be updated when the system changes. If these instructions are wrong or out of date, parts of the system may send or receive information incorrectly.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A clinician uses the system after an update. The system component instructions have not been refreshed. The system silently passes wrong or incomplete information between its parts. The clinician sees results that appear normal but are based on faulty data transfer.
update_risk.harm_description: The clinician receives inaccurate information about a patient. This could lead to a missed or delayed clinical decision. The harm is likely to be minor, but a patient could receive suboptimal care if the error is not caught.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: First, the system automatically produces a machine-readable description of how each part of the system communicates, and this is updated with every release so instructions stay current (DI-D31B359D). Second, a plain-English guide and a list of changes are published alongside every release so clinicians and support staff can see exactly what has changed and when (DI-DD2307E8). Third, every response from the AI tool includes a version label, so the support team can trace exactly which version of the system produced any given result (DI-0D26BE1B). Fourth, when clinical codes are updated, the system flags any differences and blocks the update from going live until a clinician or the support team has reviewed and resolved each change (DI-B193C816). Fifth, before any update to procedure or diagnosis codes takes effect, the team carries out an impact review and must actively approve activation (DI-337D44DE). The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs and version records each quarter to confirm all five controls are working as intended.

update_risk.title: Real patient data copied into the test environment
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-088. Workshop decision: escalate_class_C. Control adequacy: adequate. Low probability - note at workshop
update_risk.hazard_description: When the test environment is set up, it may copy real patient records from the live system. Those records are not stripped of patient details before copying. Real patient data then sits in a test environment that has weaker security controls.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A developer, tester, or other non-clinical member of staff can view or change real patient records inside the test environment. They may not realise the data is real. The data may also be shared more widely than a live record would be, for example in bug reports or log files.
update_risk.harm_description: A patient's confidential health information is seen by people who have no right to see it. This is a serious breach of patient privacy. It could cause distress, damage to reputation, or harm if sensitive information such as mental health or HIV status is disclosed without consent.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: IG/Security (GDPR + DCB0129).
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: The test environment is built using only artificial, made-up patient data. No real patient records are ever copied into it. This is enforced automatically each time the test environment is set up (DI-99A33896, DI-B8674FBF). The test environment is kept completely separate from the live system. Each part of the system stores patient information in its own dedicated, isolated area, so data cannot leak between environments (DI-AF5A1668, DI-84F44836). If the test environment is missing data for a particular area, a warning is shown to the person running the test so they know the results may be incomplete (DI-93162C3C). The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs and environment build records every quarter to confirm that no real patient data has entered the test environment.

update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: Three controls reduce this risk. First, the system uses a fixed, versioned list of error categories to classify every error into one of three groups and direct the development team to the correct fix. This list is maintained by the development team and reviewed whenever the system is updated (DI-990C0AFA). Second, every error the system returns is wrapped in a standard, consistent format with a readable error code. Third, the system allows the error category rules to be updated at any time without restarting the system, and each change is tracked with a version number. The development team manages these updates as needed (DI-770FD74A). update_risk.title: A patient data message in the wrong format breaks a clinical system that relies on it
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-091. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: adequate. Create R-LEO-AI-138
update_risk.hazard_description: This system sends patient information to other clinical systems using a standard data format called FHIR. If the system sends a message that does not follow the required format rules, the receiving clinical system may fail, show wrong information, or silently drop the data.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A clinician using a downstream system receives incomplete or missing patient information. They do not know the data is wrong or absent. They make a clinical decision based on that incomplete picture.
update_risk.harm_description: A clinician acts on missing or incorrect patient information. This could lead to a wrong or delayed diagnosis, an unsafe medicine decision, or a missed referral. The patient could come to serious harm as a result.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: First, the system automatically checks every patient data message against the required UK format rules before it is sent. This check runs every time a software change is made, without any manual step needed. This is the automated format checker built into the development process (DI-BDFF6DA7). Second, patient findings, care milestones, and audit results are each sent in a defined, structured way so receiving systems always know what to expect. The development team sets these rules and they apply to every message the system sends (DI-710D5213). Third, before any change to the AI workflow goes live, the team runs a dry-run test to confirm the new setup produces correctly formatted messages. This happens before every activation (DI-ACB587DD). Fourth, every message the system sends includes a version label for the AI component that produced it. This lets the receiving system and the safety team trace exactly which version of the AI created a given message, making it easier to spot and fix problems quickly (DI-0D26BE1B). Fifth, when a formatting or coding problem is found, a structured review checks all related messages and fixes any errors in the clinical codes used. The clinical safety team runs this review whenever a problem is reported (DI-1B8AC856). The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs from the automated format checker and any reported formatting failures every quarter to confirm these controls are working.

update_risk.title: Patient record saved without a source label
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-092. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: adequate. Create R-LEO-AI-139
update_risk.hazard_description: When the system saves a clinical finding to the patient record, it must attach a label showing where that finding came from. If this labelling step is skipped, the saved record has no source information.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A clinician reviews a finding in the patient record but cannot tell whether it came from the AI tool that reads notes, a manual entry, or another system. The clinician has no way to judge how reliable the finding is.
update_risk.harm_description: The clinician may act on a finding without knowing its origin or reliability. This could lead to a wrong or delayed clinical decision, causing serious harm to the patient.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: First, the system checks every saved record against approved UK clinical record standards and rejects any record that is missing required fields, including the source label. This check runs automatically every time a record is saved (DI-BDFF6DA7). Second, the system is designed so that every clinical finding, care milestone, and audit result must include a source label before it can be saved to the patient record. This rule is built into the system and cannot be bypassed (DI-710D5213). Third, population-level dashboards show clinicians a summary of patient findings. If source labels are missing, these dashboards will show incomplete data, making the gap visible to clinical staff who review them routinely (DI-BA2C8F3E). The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs and dashboard reports every quarter to confirm that source labels are being saved correctly on all records.

update_risk.title: Programme starts before all required setup steps are complete
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-094. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: partial. Create R-LEO-AI-140
update_risk.hazard_description: The system may allow a clinical programme to start before all required setup steps have been signed off. This means the programme could run without the correct settings, rules, or approvals being in place.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: If the programme starts too early, it may process patient records using incomplete or incorrect settings. Clinicians could receive wrong or misleading information about patients. They may act on that information without realising the programme was not ready to run.
update_risk.harm_description: A clinician could make a clinical decision based on incorrect or incomplete information produced by the programme. This could lead to a patient receiving the wrong care, a missed diagnosis, or a delayed referral. The harm could be serious.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: A six-step setup checklist must be completed before the programme can start. The system records each step as it is finished and blocks the programme from starting until all six steps are done (DI-1987BCF5). If setup is interrupted, the system saves progress so no steps are lost. An admin dashboard shows which steps are complete and which are outstanding, so the team can see at a glance what remains (DI-C58E5515). If any reference ranges are changed, the system blocks the programme from restarting until an approval record is in place. This is checked automatically each time a change is made (DI-C5A523A7). Before the programme goes live, the AI workflow runs a test check of its own settings to confirm everything is configured correctly. The programme cannot start if this test check fails (DI-ACB587DD). Any changes to the rules the AI follows must be tested in a safe trial run before they take effect. The programme is blocked from starting until this trial run passes (DI-DFAF200B). The clinical safety committee reviews whether all these controls are working as intended every quarter.

update_risk.title: Automated quality checks miss incorrectly coded clinical entries
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-008. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: gap. Split from R-LEO-AI-065 per Dedup Auditor - different control layer (automated rule vs human auditor approval).
update_risk.hazard_description: The system uses automated rules to check that clinical codes in patient records are correct. These rules have gaps. Some incorrect codes pass through the checks without being flagged for a clinician to review.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A patient's record contains an incorrect clinical code. The automated quality checks do not catch it. The code enters the patient's care record without any clinician reviewing it. Clinical decisions or care pathways may then be based on wrong information.
update_risk.harm_description: A clinician makes a clinical decision based on an incorrect code in the patient's record. The patient receives the wrong treatment, misses a needed treatment, or is placed on the wrong care pathway. This could cause serious harm.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: Four controls reduce this risk. First, the system blocks any flagged episode from being used in reports until a clinician has reviewed and resolved the flag. This runs automatically every time an episode is processed (DI-A0579B64). Second, a human-review gate stops any unreviewed episode classification from being used in audit reports. The clinical team manages this gate as part of routine reporting (DI-BD696225). Third, the system automatically checks coded patient encounters against clinical guideline rules. This runs each time a new coded entry is saved (DI-2AFF691F). Fourth, the programme team can update the guideline rule set at any time without needing a software release. This means gaps in the rules can be fixed quickly when found (DI-AA8014F9). The clinical safety committee reviews whether these controls are working every quarter.

add_fmea_item.failure_mode: Human reviewer approves a wrong replacement code during coding correction due to terminology-expertise gap
add_fmea_item.failure_effect: A human reviewer selects an incorrect SNOMED replacement during a coding-correction workflow because they lack terminology expertise or clinical context for ambiguous terms.
add_fmea_item.failure_cause: Split from R-LEO-AI-056 per Dedup Auditor - R-056 is automated dual-LLM remediation; this is human reviewer expertise gap.
add_fmea_item.recommended_actions: Additional controls required: DI for reviewer training/credentialing; DI for dual-reviewer concordance on ambiguous corrections

update_risk.title: A reviewer picks the wrong clinical code when correcting a patient record
update_risk.description: Source: FMEA_GAP. FMEA refs: FMEA-050. Workshop decision: adjust. Control adequacy: gap. Split from R-LEO-AI-056 per Dedup Auditor - R-056 is automated dual-LLM remediation; this is human reviewer expertise gap.
update_risk.hazard_description: When a clinician reviews and corrects clinical codes in a patient record, they may choose the wrong replacement code. This can happen when the correct code requires specialist terminology knowledge they do not have, or when the original note is ambiguous.
update_risk.hazardous_situation: A clinician approves an incorrect clinical code during a coding correction review. The patient record then holds the wrong diagnosis or condition code. Future clinical decisions, referrals, or medicines may be based on that wrong code without anyone realising the error.
update_risk.harm_description: The patient's record contains the wrong diagnosis or condition. A doctor or nurse reading the record may make the wrong clinical decision. This could lead to the patient receiving the wrong treatment, missing a needed treatment, or being referred along the wrong care pathway. The harm could be serious.
update_risk.identified_by: LEO-AI-CORE Hazard Workshop 2026-04-16 (facilitated by Rob Smith)
update_risk.monitoring_plan: Monitor via DQ dashboards, incident management, and quarterly RPN trend review at Clinical Safety Committee. Specialist framework: clinical safety.
update_risk.mitigation_measures_detail: Five controls reduce this risk. First, the system checks that any proposed replacement code is consistent with related codes already in the record and flags conflicts for the reviewer to consider before approving (DI-1B8AC856). This check runs automatically every time a coding correction is reviewed. Second, the AI tool that reads clinical notes is designed to preserve important detail such as whether a condition is confirmed, suspected, or ruled out, so the replacement code options shown to the reviewer reflect the correct clinical meaning (DI-6A0B55A4). This runs automatically during every AI workflow. Third, the system checks that any proposed replacement code is current and valid in the clinical coding system before showing it to the reviewer, so out-of-date or retired codes cannot be selected (DI-26CBDB16). This check runs automatically for every proposed code. Fourth, the review screen shows the reviewer how often each code has been used historically for similar patients, giving useful context to support the decision (DI-22F4E3CE). This information is displayed automatically on every coding correction review page. Fifth, the AI workflow can use two independent AI models and only suggests a replacement code when both models agree, reducing the chance of a misleading suggestion reaching the reviewer (DI-80DD8A47). This is configured by the system administrator and runs during every AI workflow. The clinical safety committee reviews audit logs and reviewer feedback every quarter to confirm all five controls are working as intended.
